correctness.rationale: The radial moments are m_j=j!Gamma(beta)/Gamma(beta+j), and Fourier coefficients of f² yield the exact normalized quartic F_beta(A,B,C), U=2beta/(beta+1), V=3beta/(beta+2), W=6beta(beta+1)/((beta+2)(beta+3)). The unique phase-sensitive term 4sqrt(U)ACB² forces b² conjugate(a*c)>0 when all modes are nonzero. On faces A=0 or C=0, switching on the missing coordinate gives a positive first variation; on B=0 the B² derivative is twice a sum of strictly positive terms involving V-1 and 2V-W for beta>1, and pure B also admits an improving perturbation. Thus no boundary optimizer. At beta=infinity, the exact SOS identity 6-F_infinity=(2sqrt2 AC-B²)²+3B⁴+8A²B²+5A⁴ has a unique normalized zero A=B=0,C=1. Its quadratic coercivity, together with finite-weight coefficient error O(beta^-1)(A²+B²), localizes global optimizers at A=O(beta^-1), B²=O(beta^-1). The scaled excess is J(t,s)=24s-4s²+4sqrt2 ts-8t², whose completion squares gives a unique value 48 at (t,s)=(sqrt2,4), producing full (not merely subsequential) coefficient limits and excess. Independent SymPy expansion verifies exact SOS, strict derivative coefficients at beta>1, and unique J maximum. Diagnostic finite optimization is not used as an infinite proof.

limitations: Only alpha>-1, standard radial power-weighted probability disk, analytic polynomials degree<=2. No finite-beta closed form or uniqueness of finite-beta magnitude triple.
